A denied access is a real access failure. Structured metadata marks it as a non-retryable permission error, so the agent does not waste retries and can report the problem.
This hides an access failure as a valid empty result. The agent would wrongly conclude that the restricted log groups contain no matching lines.
The empty result is still misclassified as a transient failure. The agent still retries and still reports an unstable service for successful queries.
A query that ran and found nothing is a valid empty result. It is a success, so it must not be flagged as a retryable failure.
Real timeouts would then be reported as empty results. The fix belongs in the tool, which must separate access failures from valid empty results.
The paths field makes a rule conditional. A path-scoped rule loads only when a matching file is edited, not at the start of every session.
The pattern **/*.test.tsx matches only files whose names end in .test.tsx. Button.tsx does not match, so the testing rule stays out of context.
Path-scoped rules load only when Claude Code edits files that match their glob patterns. Button.tsx matches none of the three patterns, so none of these rules adds context or token usage.
Path scoping keeps non-matching rules out of context, which reduces irrelevant context and token usage. Claude Code does not load every rule and then filter the rules afterward.

Direct execution suits simple, well-scoped changes. A task with an open architectural choice across many files needs plan mode, and detailed upfront instructions do not replace exploration and design.
Plan mode is designed for multi-file changes with multiple valid approaches and architectural decisions, and it allows design before committing to changes, which prevents costly rework.
